projects.description: 42 is a protocol designed to create, trade, and settle synthetic resources in the blockchain space using peer-to-peer smart contracts. Public blockchains have limited transaction capacity, leading to competition and fluctuating fees. 42 solves this problem by converting key blockchain resources, such as average transaction fees, into tradable assets, allowing for better price discovery and resource allocation. This system benefits a variety of users: miners can secure future income by selling transaction fees, service providers such as wallets and exchanges can hedge against commission volatility by buying them, and collectors can offset high mining costs. The design of the protocol allows for better prediction and management of settlement costs in the network, which changes the way blockchain networks approach resource allocation and pricing.

projects.description:
ActionModel is developing a community-owned Large Action Model (LAM), an artificial intelligence system designed to perform real-world digital tasks on computers by interacting with graphical user interfaces (GUIs), rather than just generating text like traditional Large Language Models (LLMs). It monitors screen states, decides on actions (such as clicking on coordinates, entering text, or scrolling) using its own action tree built from user input, executes those actions, and loops until the task is complete. This enables offline automation of workflows such as data entry, website navigation, or application operations without the use of APIs.

The project counteracts the centralized development of AI by large technology companies through community contributions: users install a browser extension for passive or active learning and create/sell reusable workflows on a marketplace, where their completion earns creators ongoing rewards.

Actionist's desktop application serves as a tool for user interaction, enabling the creation of specialized AI agents (digital employees with memory, schedules, personalities, and access to tools) that work locally or in the cloud around the clock, with full history tracking for transparency.

$LAM is a proprietary token that enables actions to work, rewards learning and contribution, provides governance, and represents an ownership stake in the AI system.

projects.description:
BULK is a decentralized trading system designed to bridge the speed gap between centralized and decentralized markets. The project architecture includes:

Low-latency order matching and propagation in the 5-20 ms range, with the prospect of evolving to the microsecond level.

Decentralization with no leaders, no single point of failure, leader-block producers and centralized sequencers.

Verifiability and openness, where the state of the system is cryptographically verifiable and the participation of validators is open and enforced by economic steak.

A high-performance orderbook capable of handling workloads well above current onchain systems.

BULK utilizes deterministic FIFO mapping, provides colocation-level speed through a network of validators, supports gasless orders and APIs for integration. There are no bridges or sequencers in the architecture, reducing the risks of centralization and security vulnerabilities. Solana is used to store assets and calculations, and a separate execution layer is optimized for high speed.

projects.description:
Hit is a trading platform that offers users a unique mechanism for gaining margin access to the cryptocurrency markets. Its key concept is based on "blind" position opening: the user sets the amount he is willing to risk (his bet), and the platform then randomly assigns a specific asset, leverage (up to 1000x) and direction (long or short) for this position. The user's maximum possible loss is limited to their initial bet, while the potential profit is unlimited and depends on market movements. The user retains control over the moment of exit from the position and can both increase it and fix the profit.

The platform is built using onchain technology, which makes all trades verifiable. Direct market data streams are used for pricing, and order execution aims to be instantaneous (in less than a second). The stated goal is to provide a simplified and transparent way to access high-risk trading, eliminating the need for users to analyze the market and make multiple decisions, presenting market chaos as an integral part of the experience.

projects.description:
Monaco is a decentralized trading protocol built on a central limit order book (CLOB) that connects multiple trading applications with a common liquidity layer on the blockchain infrastructure (specifically the Sei network). It handles spot and open-ended cryptocurrency markets and supports additional market types such as real asset markets and prediction markets. The design decouples the order execution engine from individual user interfaces, so different trading applications and interfaces are connected to a single engine with deep price liquidity, unified order matching, and standardized settlement.

The protocol aims to give application developers and traders access to institutional-level market depth without the need to develop proprietary matching and liquidity systems. Trades are executed quickly and settled on the network with minimal latency, and a common infrastructure can distribute commissions or order flow revenues back to applications using the protocol. Key features include support for different asset types, shared liquidity between interfaces and tools for professional and retail access through integrated interfaces.

projects.description:
Shelby is a decentralized hot storage network created by Aptos Labs in conjunction with Jump Crypto and designed for Web3 applications that require fast and frequent access to data, not just cold archival storage. Shelby supports real-time or near real-time use cases such as video streaming, generative AI pipelines, token-controlled content, dynamic NFTs, and decentralized physical infrastructure networks (DePINs) where data speed and availability are critical.

Shelby is built on a high performance foundation: low latency (reads less than a second), a dedicated fiber backbone between high-performance nodes, and an architecture optimized for fast reads and writes. The protocol separates the control and data planes, uses erasure coding (to reduce replication overhead and increase recovery throughput), and implements crypto-economic auditing to maintain data integrity without excessive overhead. Shelby supports pay-as-you-go usage and monetization of data reads, meaning nodes are rewarded for actual usage, especially for high performance. Permission logic/access control (e.g., token management, smart contract-defined permissions) and dynamic pricing or billing are part of the model.

Shelby is blockchain independent; although its own coordination/finalization layer appears to be tied to Aptos, there are plans to support multiple blockchains (Solana, Ethereum, etc.) in the future.

Its main goal is to turn complex AI-related tasks such as model evaluation, testing and adversarial data generation into accessible consumer applications. The platform allows real users to contribute feedback and behavioral data needed to improve AI systems. These contributions are recorded as verifiable artifacts on the blockchain. The project targets both non-technical users who can participate through engaging applications and developers who can create, share and monetize AI models within an open ecosystem.

On the technical side, Stormrae works through a modular participation architecture that connects consumer activity with enterprise AI development processes. The platform tracks user contributions through Shards (Shards - units of participation) and Echoes (activity signals), which form a verifiable contribution history on the Solana blockchain.
